tips.title: Same note, higher
tips.text: Octave: 2 strings up, 2 frets to the right (3 frets if you land on the B or high E string).
tips.example: C on the A string fret 3, then C on the G string fret 5; G on the D string fret 5, then G on the B string fret 8.
tips.memo: 2 strings, 2 frets. Three frets if you land on B or high E.

tips.title: The next string over
tips.text: Same note on the neighbouring higher string: go back 5 frets toward the headstock (4 frets from the G string).
tips.example: A on the low E string fret 5 = the open A string; D on the G string fret 7 = D on the B string fret 3.
tips.memo: Five frets back, four from G.

tips.title: Tuning by ear
tips.text: Fret 5 gives the neighbouring open string (fret 4 on the G string).
tips.example: Low E fret 5 = A; A fret 5 = D; D fret 5 = G; G fret 4 = B; B fret 5 = high E.

tips.title: Fourth, then fifth
tips.text: Next string up, same fret = a fourth (a major third from G). Two frets further = a fifth (3 from G).
tips.example: A string fret 3 = C; D string fret 3 = F, fret 5 = G.
tips.memo: Same fret: fourth. Two frets more: fifth.

tips.title: The mirror
tips.text: Low E and high E carry the same notes at every fret.
tips.memo: Learn one string, you know two.

tips.title: Landmarks on the low E string
tips.example: The inlay dots fall on 3, 5, 7 and 12.
tips.memo: F G A B C D E: frets 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12.

tips.title: On a single string
tips.text: Minor third 3 frets, major third 4, fifth 7, octave 12.
tips.example: G fret 3, then B fret 7 (major third).

tips.title: E–F and B–C
tips.text: Only one fret between these two pairs, two frets everywhere else.
tips.example: Low E string: E 0, F 1; B 7, C 8.
tips.memo: E and F, B and C: neighbours.

tips.title: Order of inversions
tips.text: On the G, B, high E strings, going up: root position, 1st inversion, 2nd inversion, then it starts again 12 frets later.
tips.example: G major: 1st inversion at fret 4, 2nd at fret 7, root position at fret 12.

tips.title: Major pentatonic
tips.text: Major pentatonic = minor pentatonic 3 frets lower.
tips.example: C major uses the A minor pentatonic (frets 5 to 8 on the low E string).
tips.memo: It is the minor, 3 frets lower.

tips.title: Capo
tips.text: Capo n + shape of X = X raised by n semitones.
tips.memo: Capo 2: the G shape sounds A.

tips.title: Going minor
tips.text: Lower the third by one fret.
tips.example: E major to E minor: the G string goes from fret 1 to open.
tips.memo: Third lowered by one fret: minor.

tips.title: The degrees
tips.text: In a major key: 1, 4 and 5 are major; 2, 3 and 6 are minor; 7 is diminished.
tips.example: In A: A, Bm, C♯m, D, E, F♯m.
